name: Chestnut: long stem
summary: Red-only light during fruiting for longer, heavier stems, the crunchy part chefs want from chestnut mushrooms.
notes: Caps may sit a little smaller than on the free card. Pick before the veil tears.
chamber_notes: Chamber limits: there is no heater or cooler, so temperature targets only hold if the room sits near them. There is no CO2 sensor, so the fan schedule stands in for fresh air. The humidifier can only add moisture, so a low humidity target depends on dry room air.

source_notes.title: Liu et al. 2024, Pholiota adiposa light quality
source_notes.detail: Liu Y. et al., Spectroscopy and Spectral Analysis 44(08), 2024. In a 12 h light plant factory, pure red light raised stipe growth by 78.4% and fruit mass by 90.0% compared with white light. Blue light made thicker stipes and wider caps instead.

source_notes.title: Stamets
source_notes.detail: Paul Stamets, Growing Gourmet and Medicinal Mushrooms (commonly cited chamber ranges). Related Pholiota spp. like cool, wet fruiting conditions.

light_recipe.why: Pure red gave 78.4% more stipe growth and 90% more fruit mass than white in Liu 2024. Pinning keeps the free card light.
light_recipe.wavelength_note: WS2812 red is roughly 620 to 630 nm and blue roughly 465 to 475 nm. The RGB mix is an approximation of the cited wavelengths, not a measured spectrum. RGB percent is LED drive level, not a photon ratio.
